plan.planning_summary: The previous route failed compilation because it attempted to optimize two distinct layer topologies (SiO2/TiO2 and TiO2/SiO2) simultaneously within a single request. The TMM solver requires a fixed, explicit stack topology for optimization. To resolve this, I am splitting the problem into two sequential, deterministic routes. This response defines Route A, which fixes the topology as Air | SiO2 | TiO2 | Glass. It optimizes the thickness of these two layers within the 40-160 nm bounds to minimize mean reflectance. If this route yields valid candidates, a subsequent refinement can address the inverted order.

routes.title: Optimization of Air/SiO2/TiO2/Glass Two-Layer AR Coating
routes.scientific_hypothesis: For a two-layer system with SiO2 (n=1.46) and TiO2 (n=2.40) on glass (n=1.52), the specific ordering of Low-High index (SiO2 then TiO2) admits a global minimum in mean reflectance over 450-700 nm within the 40-160 nm thickness constraints that is distinct from the High-Low ordering.
routes.design_principle: Impedance matching via sequential quarter-wave-like transformations, where the low-index layer acts as an intermediate transformer between air and the high-index layer, which then matches to the substrate.
routes.proposed_topology: Air (n=1.0) | Layer 1: SiO2 (n=1.46) | Layer 2: TiO2 (n=2.40) | Substrate: Glass (n=1.52). Total finite layers: 2.
soft_objectives: minimize arithmetic mean power reflectance from 450 to 700 nm
achieve mean reflectance below 0.03 as a soft scoring preference
manufacturing_considerations: layer thickness must be between 40 and 160 nm
exactly one layer of SiO2 and one layer of TiO2 in this specific order
theory_basis: Transfer Matrix Method for multilayer interference
Quarter-wave antireflection coating theory generalized for two layers
expected_advantages: Provides a definitive optimal solution for the Low-High index sequence
Resolves the compilation ambiguity by fixing the topology
Allows direct comparison with the inverted sequence in a future step
known_risks: The global minimum for this specific order might exceed the 0.03 soft target due to material index mismatch
Thickness constraints (40-160 nm) may prevent reaching the ideal quarter-wave optical thickness for the center wavelength
routes.execution_request_english: Perform a deterministic optimization using the Transfer Matrix Method for s-polarized light at normal incidence (0 degrees). The stack consists of exactly two finite layers on a semi-infinite glass substrate (n=1.52, lossless) with air incidence (n=1.0). The layer order is fixed: Layer 1 is SiO2 (n=1.46, lossless) and Layer 2 is TiO2 (n=2.40, lossless). Optimize the thickness of Layer 1 and Layer 2, both bounded between 40 nm and 160 nm. The objective is to minimize the arithmetic mean power reflectance sampled from 450 nm to 700 nm at 5 nm intervals. Use seed 17 for the optimizer and allow a maximum of 64 solver evaluations. Output the optimal thicknesses, the full reflectance spectrum, and the calculated mean reflectance. Canonical user controls: incidence angles 0 degrees. polarization s. wavelength intervals 450-700 nm. soft objectives: minimize arithmetic mean power reflectance from 450 to 700 nm; achieve mean reflectance below 0.03 as a soft scoring preference. behaviors to suppress or avoid: high reflection in the 450 to 700 nm band. manufacturing constraints: layer thickness must be between 40 and 160 nm; exactly one layer of SiO2 and one layer of TiO2.
routes.revision_reason: Split the ambiguous dual-topology request from route_01 into a single, fixed topology (Air/SiO2/TiO2/Glass) to satisfy the TMM compiler requirement for an explicit layer stack. This addresses the compilation failure while preserving the scientific intent to find the best geometry.

Whether the 0.03 mean reflectance target is physically achievable with either order given the 40-160 nm thickness constraints.
